terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.
